argument_summary: The certification defense should be narrowed. The admissible record supports that the current release passes aggregate readiness by 2.1 percentage points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and can be described using public governance guidance that expects current evaluation results, limitations, and monitoring to be documented. The same record also shows the small-business onboarding slice is currently below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, and neither prior approval nor the informal monitoring comment substitutes for current disclosure or approved mitigation. On that basis, the supportable position is not clean compliance; it is a caveated certification packet that explicitly presents the subgroup regression as a material current limitation rather than implying the issue is already resolved.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is relied on here.
claims_about_policy: Policy supports only a narrow, caveated certification framing on this record. The controlling rule is that current release documentation must reflect current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance. The admissible evidence does not show approved mitigation or formal acceptance, so prior approval and informal monitoring can be used only as context. The defensible policy claim is therefore that certification is arguable only if the packet is treated as caveated and the subgroup regression is expressly identified as a current material limitation for the named use case.
concessions: The current record does not establish clean compliance because it does not include evidence of approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or owner-accepted exception for the subgroup regression.
Prior approval of the same model family is stale context only because it predates the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not policy-equivalent to approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance.
Without evidence that the current release documentation reflects the subgroup regression, any stronger certification claim would overstate what the record proves.
